text:
Maria L: quick question — for multi-region hosted routing, are we still leaning on strict lowest-latency region or switching to a hedged-tier approach? need to nail down fallback behavior for model variants too

Josh K: leaning hedged-tier for Standard customers, yes. Enterprise stays sticky by region unless region degraded. hedging = send 2 probes and pick first healthy response. reduces tail latency spikes :thinking_face:

Samir: +1 for hedging but we need clear cost guardrails. hedging can double token cost in worst case. propose: hedging only for requests under 2s expected compute + only for premium traffic or p95 SLA buckets.

Dana P: can we express that as routing policy in the console? something like:
```yaml
routing: 
  prefer: region
  fallback: hedged
  hedging:
    enabled: true
    max_extra_requests: 1
    tiers: [enterprise, premium]
    max_expected_latency_ms: 2000
```
That would make UX actionable.

Alex: I like that. also need explicit model-variant fallback path. if region A has model v1 (fp16) and region B only has quantized v1-q4, we should have policy to prefer same quality, else allow variant with explicit quality penalty and flag in response headers.

Keval: +1. internal API debate: should routing return region hint and chosen_variant in the routing metadata field, or just surface selected endpoint? monitoring wants both.

Infra Bot: deploy-bot: canary routing-service v2.3 -> staging started at 1759001260

Josh K: metadata only. return both region_hint and final_region + variant in headers and trace. clients can opt-in to get region_hint. default keep minimal.

Maria L: telemetry question — what panels should go live for SRE/product to understand hedging impact? p50/p95/p99 latency by region, cost-per-1000 tokens by region+tier, hedged-request-rate, hedged-success-first-byte-rate?

Samir: add 'variant-fallback-rate' (percent of requests that used downgraded quantized variant), 'quality-regression-alerts' tied to evals, and 'hedge-cancel-lag' (how long before hedged duplicate was cancelled).

Dana P: UI idea — in rollout modal add a toggle: "Allow cross-region variant downgrade" with explanatory tooltip: "Enabling lets requests failover to compatible quantized variants in other regions when primary region lacks capacity. Quality tradeoff applies."

Alex: implementation note — runtime must support in-flight cache transfer avoidance. when we fall back to other region, don't attempt KV cache revives. just set cold-start penalty metric.

Keval: regarding quotas: if enterprise has dedicated quota in region A but hedging sends to region B, do we consume from region A quota or from tenant global quota? This matters for billing and fairness.

Josh K: proposal: consume from originating region's quota if possible; if fallback region is used due to capacity, bill fallbacks to a separate "fallback-bucket" that is visible to tenant. console shows fallback consumption.

Maria L: sounds reasonable. Dana can you update the console mockups and add a tiny panel for fallback-bucket usage and a per-tenant toggle to opt-out?

Dana P: will do. will add tooltip copy for billing and quality.

Samir: operational runbook: if variant-fallback-rate > 5% for >10m trigger paging to infra and trigger automated capacity spin-up in preferred region. we should simulate this in chaos tests.

Infra Bot: chaos-sim: region-hedge-sim started (expected runtime 15m)

Maria L: action items: 1) Dana update UX mock and new toggle 2) Josh/Keval finalize header schema (region_hint, final_region, variant_id, variant_quality_score) 3) Samir infra: add metrics (variant-fallback-rate, hedge-cancel-lag) 4) Alex runtime: ensure cold-start flag for cross-region fallbacks 5) Keval billing: add fallback-bucket accounting

Josh K: I'll draft the header schema in eng-platform PR and ping folks for review.

Keval: ping me when PR is up, I'll validate billing implications.

Maria L: thanks all — we'll sync in weekly routing triage tomorrow. :thumbsup:
